web.description: A malicious widget can bypass the security filter that Telegram added to its Android app last week and run code outside it, according to NebuSec , a security company.   Widgets are small interactive blocks that bots send inside chat messages, and their JavaScript runs on the user's phone. The researchers ran their demonstration on a Telegram test server, because only approved bots can send widgets on the live service now.   Bots could start sending widgets last week. Two days later, an account called V12 posted a video on X claiming that any Telegram message could now be used to execute remote code. web.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
web.description: Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it.   In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool. They even labeled it a security fix. Teams pinned to it would have passed every check.   The trick works because GitHub lets copies of a project, called forks, share code with the original. In May, the same technique hit the popular actions-cool/issues-helper tool, stealing credentials from the pipelines that ran it.   The lesson: pinning guarantees the code won't change, but not who wrote it.   That gap is the focus of an upcoming webinar, GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning .
